export const meta = {
  name: 'phase1-core',
  description: 'Phase 1: model layer + journal, context/sandbox/verdict/ports, runtime integration, adversarial review and fix',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Modules', detail: 'model layer+journal || context/sandbox/verdict/ports' },
    { title: 'Integrate', detail: 'agent/code/verify nodes, escalation, replay, verdicts in the runtime' },
    { title: 'Extend', detail: 'parallel map, timers/tick, label policy, CLI' },
    { title: 'Review', detail: 'three-lens adversarial review' },
    { title: 'Fix', detail: 'fix confirmed findings' },
  ],
}
const COMMON = `Repository /home/user/workflow-foundry (Node 24.21 on PATH; ESM; node:test; deps pinned: ajv 8.20.0 is available; do NOT add npm dependencies; do NOT git commit). READ research/core-20261006/DESIGN.md FIRST — it is the binding spec for this phase; follow its field names exactly. Also read policy/models.json. Existing runtime: src/runtime.mjs (durable DAG runner over SQLite in src/store.mjs), src/validate.mjs, src/dataflow.mjs, src/data.mjs (digest, canonical, resolve refs, condition, FoundryError). Match the surrounding code style (dense ESM, FoundryError codes, no comments where obvious). Never weaken existing tests. The full default suite (npm test) must stay green except for pre-existing environment skips; live-model tests must be opt-in via env FOUNDRY_LIVE_MODELS=1 and skip with a precise reason otherwise. Never print env var values or read credential files. Local open-weight models: llama-server binary at /opt/llamacpp/build/bin/llama-server, weights in /opt/models (see policy/models.json); hosted Claude models via the 'claude' CLI (see DESIGN §2). Report: files changed, exact test counts, deviations from DESIGN.md with reasons.`

phase('Modules')
const [models, ctx] = await parallel([
  () => agent(`${COMMON}
TASK: the model layer and journal (DESIGN §2, §3). You own NEW files: src/models/policy.mjs, src/models/port.mjs, src/models/providers/claude-cli.mjs, src/models/providers/llama-server.mjs, src/models/providers/scripted.mjs, src/models/llama-supervisor.mjs, src/journal.mjs, tests/models-policy.test.mjs, tests/models-port.test.mjs, tests/models-live.test.mjs, tests/journal.test.mjs. Do not edit runtime.mjs/store.mjs (journal.mjs takes a node:sqlite DatabaseSync handle, e.g. store.db, and creates its own tables with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS).
Requirements:
- policy.mjs: loadPolicy(path default <repo>/policy/models.json) returns {policy, hash}; validates structure; resolve/classIndex/nextClass/modelsForClass; MODEL_NOT_IN_POLICY for unknown ids. Test that a scripted provider is never called with an id outside the policy ("no model id outside this file" test, ROADMAP §2.3).
- port.mjs ModelPort({policy, providers:{name: provider}, journal, mode:'live'|'replay'|'replay-or-live', salt}) .call(req) per DESIGN §2/§3, including Ajv validation of value vs schema, portable-schema-subset check (DESIGN §5.3) before any provider call (UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA), replay key, journaling of every call (ok or error) BEFORE returning, error classification, per-provider concurrency semaphores, cost accounting (costUsd for hosted, imputedUsd for local via policy rate), lookup by (runId,nodeKey,attempt) for crash recovery (journal.forAttempt). 
- claude-cli.mjs: spawn the 'claude' binary (configurable path) with policy.providers['claude-cli'].invocation + --model, --system-prompt, --json-schema, --effort (none->low? map: none|low->low, medium->medium, high->high), --max-budget-usd (per-call cap, default 1), prompt on stdin, cwd = a fresh empty temp dir (removed after), timeout with process-group kill, parse JSON result: structured_output, result, total_cost_usd, usage (input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens), is_error/api_error_status/subtype/stop_reason/terminal_reason; classify 429/529/overloaded/rate as MODEL_RATE_LIMIT. Record engineVersion from 'claude --version' (cached once). Never pass --fallback-model. Inherit process.env (the CLI needs its managed auth) but never log it.
- llama-server.mjs + llama-supervisor.mjs: as DESIGN §2; ensureServer starts the server detached with -c 8192 -t 4 -np 1 --jinja on the policy port if /health is not ok, waits up to 120 s; stopServer; engineVersion from 'llama-server --version'. Request with temperature (default 0), max_tokens, response_format json_schema strict, chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking.
- scripted.mjs: ScriptedProvider(fn or table) with call log for tests.
- journal.mjs per DESIGN §3 (model_calls table + indexes; record, lookup(replayKey), forAttempt(runId,nodeKey,attempt), forRun(runId), costForRun(runId)).
- Tests (default suite, no network): policy validation; replay determinism (live then replay gives identical values and zero provider calls); strict replay miss -> REPLAY_MISS; resample changes key; schema-invalid provider output -> MODEL_SCHEMA journaled; unsupported schema keyword rejected before call; concurrency cap respected; cost accounting.
- tests/models-live.test.mjs (opt-in FOUNDRY_LIVE_MODELS=1): one Haiku structured call via claude-cli; one local call via llama-server on qwen3.5-2b-q4km. RUN THIS LIVE TEST ONCE YOURSELF with FOUNDRY_LIVE_MODELS=1 and report its output (cost, latency, values). Stop any llama-server you started when done.`, { label: 'models+journal', phase: 'Modules' }),
  () => agent(`${COMMON}
TASK: context compiler, sandbox, verdicts, ports, identity/decision schemas (DESIGN §1.2, §4, §5.2, §5.3, §6). You own NEW files: src/context.mjs, src/sandbox.mjs, src/verdict.mjs, src/ports.mjs, src/schema-subset.mjs (portable subset checker of DESIGN §5.3, exported as checkPortableSchema(schema) and quarantine check checkQuarantinedSchema(schema)), schemas/identity.schema.json, schemas/decision.schema.json, tests/context.test.mjs, tests/sandbox.test.mjs, tests/verdict.test.mjs, tests/ports.test.mjs. Do not edit existing files.
Requirements:
- context.mjs compileContext exactly per DESIGN §4 (deterministic, byte-identical for identical inputs; canonical JSON rendering; token estimate ceil(utf8 bytes/4); per-input truncation marker; CONTEXT_OVERFLOW vs truncate lowest priority first; receipt + receiptHash + promptHash; label join; quarantined declassification; retryNote section). Tests: byte-identical determinism, any input change changes receiptHash, truncation, overflow fail, untrusted preamble present, label joins, quarantined declassify.
- sandbox.mjs runCode({lang:'js'|'python', source, input, timeoutMs, maxOutputBytes}) per DESIGN §1.2: user+net+mount namespaces via 'unshare --user --map-root-user --net --mount --fork', tmpfs over /home /root /opt/models /tmp /var inside the namespace, clean env (PATH only), code and input passed via stdin (no files in visible dirs), JS via node --permission (deny fs write/child_process/worker) with an ESM loader that imports the user module from a data: URL or similar and calls default export main(input) (await if async), Python via python3 -I -c runner calling main(input); output JSON on stdout last line marker; errors -> CODE_ERROR (with truncated stderr), CODE_TIMEOUT, CODE_OUTPUT; SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE if unshare fails (never fall back to unsandboxed). Tests: js and python pure functions; async js; timeout kills; network blocked (attempt a TCP connect / fetch -> fails); cannot read /home/user/workflow-foundry/package.json; cannot write outside; huge output rejected; exception -> CODE_ERROR.
- verdict.mjs: verdictOf(run) mapping table of DESIGN §5.2, plus AUTHORITY mapping and the authority flags; tests for every row.
- ports.mjs: ContextPort/EffectPort/JudgmentPort per DESIGN §6 with native implementations (JudgmentPort engines 'rule' (function returning probabilities) and 'model' (uses a ModelPort-like object with call(); enum schema; returns chosen + self-reported confidence; probabilities = one-hot smoothed by confidence) — keep it small; tests with a fake model object).
- schemas: identity and decision JSON Schemas (draft-07) per DESIGN §6, plus tests that valid examples pass and invalid ones fail using ajv.`, { label: 'context+sandbox+verdict+ports', phase: 'Modules' }),
])

phase('Integrate')
const integ = await agent(`${COMMON}
Two module agents just finished. Their reports:
--- models+journal ---
${models}
--- context+sandbox+verdict+ports ---
${ctx}
TASK: integrate into the runtime (DESIGN §1.1–1.3, §1.5, §5.1, §5.2, §6). You own: schemas/workflow.schema.json, src/validate.mjs, src/dataflow.mjs, src/runtime.mjs, src/store.mjs, src/engine.mjs, src/foundry.mjs, and NEW tests tests/runtime-agent.test.mjs, tests/runtime-code-verify.test.mjs, tests/runtime-replay.test.mjs. You may make small compatible fixes in the new src/models/*, src/context.mjs, src/sandbox.mjs, src/verdict.mjs if needed (say so).
- Schema: add node kinds agent, code, verify with their fields (allOf required-field rules), top-level labels and discovery; validate.mjs 'fields' map for the new kinds; validator checks: agent returns/verify output schemas pass checkPortableSchema; quarantined schemas pass checkQuarantinedSchema; model.id must exist in the policy and model.class/maxClass are valid classes with class<=maxClass (validator receives the policy via options.modelPolicy; if absent and the workflow has agent nodes, error MODEL_POLICY_REQUIRED); inspectRefs must cover context.inputs[].ref (refs in DESIGN use plain strings like "item" or "nodes.x.y" — normalise them to the {$ref} form internally), checks (with 'output' as an allowed local root inside agent checks), subject, args. dataflow.mjs: output schemas for agent (returns), code (returns or unknown), verify (fixed record).
- engine.mjs: add the new semantic modules (context.mjs, verdict.mjs, sandbox.mjs, schema-subset.mjs, models/port.mjs, journal.mjs) to the engine identity file list.
- Runtime: constructor options {models, modelPolicy, codeRunner?} ; create() records modelPolicyHash, assignment/assignmentHash, sampleSalt, modelMode, identity envelope (validated against schemas/identity.schema.json) in run.extra or dedicated fields; execute() refuses MODEL_POLICY_DRIFT. agent execution + escalation exactly per DESIGN §5.1 (E1, E2, E7; outages never escalate), journaling via ModelPort, context.compiled event (receipt) before each call, model.escalated events and decision records (decisions table in store.mjs), cost charged to run.cost with budget checks, crash recovery from the journal (inject a test-only crash hook like the existing crashAfterTool, e.g. extra.crashAfterModel=nodeKey, to prove a resumed run does not call the provider again). code nodes via sandbox.runCode with returns validation. verify nodes (code/agent/capability methods, independence enforcement for different-model, gate semantics, VERIFY_FAILED). Run-level verdict via verdictOf stored on the run and emitted as run.verdict event, for both success and failure paths.
- Tests (scripted provider, no network): end-to-end workflow with code -> agent -> verify; E1 schema retry then escalation with events; E2 check-fail escalation; E7 cap; outage -> env_fault with no escalation; replay: a second run in replay mode with the same salt reproduces outputs with zero provider calls and byte-identical receipts; crash after model call resumes from journal; budget exhaustion -> inconclusive; model id outside policy rejected at validation; different-model independence enforced; quarantined schema enforced.
Run npm test; everything pre-existing must still pass.`, { label: 'runtime-integration', phase: 'Integrate' })

phase('Extend')
const ext = await agent(`${COMMON}
The runtime integration agent reported:
${integ}
TASK: parallel map, timers, label policy, CLI (DESIGN §1.4, §1.5 labels, §4 label rule, §5.4). You own: schemas/workflow.schema.json, src/runtime.mjs, src/store.mjs, src/validate.mjs, src/dataflow.mjs, bin/foundry.mjs, src/foundry.mjs, src/http.mjs (only to call the timer scan from serve), and NEW tests tests/runtime-map-parallel.test.mjs, tests/timers.test.mjs, tests/labels.test.mjs, tests/cli-models.test.mjs.
- map: concurrency + failure fail_fast|collect with per-item isolation (one item's failure must not abort the invocation in collect mode; refactor the invocation-wide abort into scoped controllers as needed), outputs ordered by index, resume mid-map re-enters only incomplete items, semaphore still bounds concurrent capability/model calls. Tests: max in-flight observed == concurrency; completion order shuffled but outputs index-ordered; collect yields $error entries and failed count; fail_fast cancels siblings; resume after crash mid-map.
- timers: timers table; wait nodes register wake_at; Store.dueTimers(now); foundry tick --workspace W resumes due runs (new Runtime instance), serve scans every N seconds. Tests including restart (new process/Runtime).
- labels: top-level labels; static propagation through refs (agent output label = join of input labels unless quarantined; code/task outputs = join of referenced labels); reject effectful task args depending on untrusted outputs unless capability.requiresApproval (LABEL_POLICY). Tests.
- CLI: 'foundry run' accepts --policy (default policy/models.json), --model-mode, --salt, --max-cost, --assignment <json file>; new 'foundry tick' and 'foundry calls --run <id>' (lists journaled model calls with cost); help text updated.
Run npm test (must stay green).`, { label: 'map+timers+labels+cli', phase: 'Extend' })

phase('Review')
const LENSES = [
  ['replay-and-durability', 'Replay rules R1–R8 (research/landscape-20261006/09-context-async-cheap-models.md §B3) and durability: journal-before-observe, replay keys, crash recovery, idempotency, map resume ordering, timer wake after restart, engine/policy drift detection. Write a failing test for every real bug you find.'],
  ['security-and-labels', 'Sandbox escape (can code nodes read the repo, beds/, policy, other runs, network, env vars?), label policy bypasses, quarantined schema bypasses, untrusted text reaching instructions/system prompt, oracle/grader isolation, secrets in journals/events, unbounded resource use. Write a failing test or a concrete repro for every real issue.'],
  ['spec-and-semantics', 'Conformance to research/core-20261006/DESIGN.md and ROADMAP §2.1–§2.6 (field names, escalation E1/E2/E7, verdict table, portable schema subset, cost accounting incl. failed calls, decision records, identity envelope), plus correctness of concurrency (parallel map + semaphore + abort scopes) and the claude-cli/llama-server providers (error classification, timeouts, process cleanup).'],
]
const reviews = await parallel(LENSES.map(([name, lens]) => () => agent(`${COMMON}
You are an adversarial reviewer (lens: ${name}). The Phase 1 changes are in the working tree (git diff, plus new untracked files under src/, tests/, schemas/). Do NOT fix product code; you may add NEW test files named tests/review-${name}.test.mjs that demonstrate real bugs (they may fail). Focus: ${lens}
Return a JSON-ish list of findings: {severity: critical|high|medium|low, file, line, problem, repro (test name or command), suggested fix}. Only report issues you have confirmed by reading code paths or running a repro; no speculation.`, { label: `review:${name}`, phase: 'Review' })))

phase('Fix')
const fix = await agent(`${COMMON}
Three adversarial reviewers reported:
${reviews.map((r, i) => `--- ${LENSES[i][0]} ---\n${r}`).join('\n')}
TASK: for every critical/high/medium finding, verify it yourself; if real, fix it in product code and make the reviewer's repro test pass (keep their test files; fix them only if the test itself is wrong, and say why). Low findings: fix if cheap, else list as debt. Then run npm test and report exact counts, every fix, every rejected finding with reason, and remaining debt.`, { label: 'fix-findings', phase: 'Fix' })
return { models, ctx, integ, ext, reviews, fix }

result.models:
Model layer and journal are done. The default suite is green: 669 tests, 652 pass, 0 fail, 17 skipped. That is the 15 environment and opt-in skips that were already there, plus the 2 new live tests. The live test passed when I ran it with `FOUNDRY_LIVE_MODELS=1`, and no llama-server is left running.

**Files** (all new and in my scope; I edited no other file and made no commit):
- /home/user/workflow-foundry/src/models/policy.mjs
- /home/user/workflow-foundry/src/models/port.mjs
- /home/user/workflow-foundry/src/models/providers/claude-cli.mjs
- /home/user/workflow-foundry/src/models/providers/llama-server.mjs
- /home/user/workflow-foundry/src/models/providers/scripted.mjs
- /home/user/workflow-foundry/src/models/llama-supervisor.mjs
- /home/user/workflow-foundry/src/journal.mjs
- /home/user/workflow-foundry/tests/models-policy.test.mjs (6 tests)
- /home/user/workflow-foundry/tests/models-port.test.mjs (14 tests)
- /home/user/workflow-foundry/tests/journal.test.mjs (5 tests)
- /home/user/workflow-foundry/tests/models-live.test.mjs (2 tests, skipped by default with a precise reason)

Your WIP snapshot commit 2a4bde3 picked up early versions of `src/journal.mjs` and `src/models/policy.mjs`; the working tree has newer ones.

**Test counts**
- My new files: 25 pass with no network, using scripted doubles plus fake `claude` and `llama-server` scripts. The 2 live tests skip unless opted in.
- Baseline before I started: 605 tests, 590 pass, 15 skipped. The rest of the growth to 669 comes from test files other agents added while I worked.

**Live run (`FOUNDRY_LIVE_MODELS=1`, both lanes, once)**

| | Haiku via claude CLI | Local qwen3.5-2b-q4km |
|---|---|---|
| Value | `{"label":"positive","confidence":0.99}` | `{"label":"positive","confidence":0.95}` |
| Cost | $0.00391 | $0, imputed $0.000243 |
| Latency | 6089 ms | 4381 ms (2066 ms of it server start) |
| Tokens in / out | 1830 / 416 | 71 / 16 |
| Engine | claude-code 2.1.291 | llama-server 0.5.0-dev (build 1, commit 0c1e570) |

- **Haiku:** the CLI's `modelUsage` confirmed it served the requested model. A strict replay gave the identical value at $0.
- **Local:** the server was started on demand. A second call on the warm server took 1386 ms (imputed $0.000077). The server was stopped afterwards.
- **Re-check:** I changed the supervisor after that run, so I re-ran only the local lane (no hosted spend). It passed with the same values. Latency was 13.5 s, with an 11.3 s start, and the warm call took 47 s. Other agents' processes were using the CPU at the time (load average 4.9 on 4 cores, 0.33 tokens/s). Local latency and imputed cost are therefore not stable on this shared host.
- **Hosted spend:** about $0.0064 in total, including one manual Haiku probe ($0.0025) I made before writing the provider.

**Deviations from DESIGN.md**
1. **New error code `MODEL_BUDGET`:** used when the claude CLI hits its per-call `--max-budget-usd` cap. Calling that a timeout or protocol error would be misleading.
2. **Errors that throw instead of returning `ok:false`:** `MODEL_NOT_IN_POLICY`, `UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA`, `INVALID_SCHEMA`, `MODEL_REQUEST`, `MODEL_PROVIDER_MISSING` and `REPLAY_MISS` throw before any provider call and are not journaled. A cancelled call is journaled and then throws. If `REPLAY_MISS` were returned as `ok:false`, the runtime's escalation loop would wrongly escalate on it.
3. **Replay hits get their own journal row:** the row belongs to the replaying run, with cost 0 and a pointer to the original. The table has no `replayed` column, so the pointer lives in the request/response JSON.
4. **Only model-behaviour failures replay:** schema, truncation and refusal failures replay as recorded. Rate limits, outages, timeouts, protocol, budget and cancellation are journaled but never served from the journal.
5. **Crash recovery is automatic in live mode:** an identical call already journaled for the same run, node and attempt is returned as `recovered:true`, with no new provider call. `port.recover()` also exposes the rows directly.
6. **Decoding settings are normalised before hashing**, and unknown decoding fields are rejected. Leaving a field out and setting its default give the same replay key.
7. **claude-cli details:**
   - `maxTokens` and temperature can't be set on this route; both are recorded as `provider-default`.
   - Repository credentials (GH_TOKEN and similar, same list as `src/executors/claude-code.mjs`) are removed from the inherited environment.
   - If the CLI reports serving a different model than requested, the call fails as `MODEL_PROTOCOL`.
8. **llama-server details:**
   - Server start-up time counts toward the first call's latency and imputed cost; it is recorded separately in the journal.
   - The port must be serving the policy's weights file, otherwise `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE`.
   - Servers bind to loopback only and get a minimal environment (`PATH`, `LANG`).
   - A pid file lets a later supervisor stop a server left behind by a crash, and started servers are stopped on process exit.
   - `max_tokens` defaults to 1024.
9. **The portable-schema check reuses `src/schema-subset.mjs`:** that file was written by another agent and is not yet committed. I use its allowlist but throw `UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA` (its own wrapper throws `SCHEMA_NOT_PORTABLE`), so one allowlist serves both the validator and the port. Port.mjs now depends on that uncommitted file.
10. **Smaller choices:**
    - The policy hash is computed over canonical JSON, not raw file bytes.
    - `nextClass` skips classes that have no models.
    - Call results carry extra fields: `replayKey`, `promptHash`, `journalId`, and `replayedFrom` or `recovered`.
    - When a provider reports no cost, cache tokens are priced at the input rate, so the estimate errs high.
11. **"No model id outside this file" test:** it scans `src/`. It exempts only the old `src/ollama-local.mjs` adapter (`qwen3.5-9b:itb`), which the model port never reaches.
12. **Stale test name in `policy/models.json`:** its notes cite `tests/model-policy.test.mjs`, but the file is `tests/models-policy.test.mjs` as instructed. I left the policy file unedited.
result.ctx:
I've built all five modules, both schemas and the four test files. The sandbox tests found a real escape in my first version, which is now fixed. No existing files were edited and nothing was committed.

**Tests**
- My four files: 38 tests, 38 pass, 0 skipped. I ran them three times and they passed each time.
  - `tests/context.test.mjs`: 12, including the portable-subset and quarantine checks.
  - `tests/sandbox.test.mjs`: 11.
  - `tests/verdict.test.mjs`: 8.
  - `tests/ports.test.mjs`: 7, including the identity and decision schemas checked with ajv.
- Full `npm test`: 670 tests, 653 pass, 0 fail, 17 skipped. All 17 skips are existing opt-in or environment lanes. Two of them are a sibling agent's `FOUNDRY_LIVE_MODELS=1` tests. My tests use no live models; the judgment port is tested with a fake model.

**The escape I found and fixed.** This environment runs as uid 0, so "root" inside the sandbox maps to real host root. In my first version, Python code could:
- unmount the `/home` mask and read the repository;
- switch `/` back to writable and write `/opt/...` as host root.

I confirmed this with a probe, then deleted the probe file. The interpreter now runs one namespace deeper as an unprivileged user with no capabilities. The kernel then locks every mount it inherits, so it can no longer undo the masks or the read-only setting. A regression test checks this.

**Where I went beyond or interpreted DESIGN.md**
1. **Sandbox (`src/sandbox.mjs`):**
   - Adds a PID namespace with its own `/proc`, so a timeout or cancel also kills forked or `setsid` children. A test confirms the child exists first, then that it dies.
   - Makes every inherited mount read-only.
   - Hides `/run` as well as the five paths in DESIGN.
   - Node gets no file reads at all, which is stricter than "no fs write".
   - `/tmp` is a writable 16 MiB scratch area; the other masks are read-only.
   - `runCode` returns `{value, stderr, elapsedMs}`, since DESIGN doesn't fix a return shape.
   - Adds error codes `CODE_LANG`, `CODE_SOURCE`, `CODE_TIMEOUT_INVALID`, `CODE_OUTPUT_INVALID` and `CANCELLED`.
   - Adds an `unshare` path override (used to test `SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE`) and `sandboxStatus()`.
2. **Context compiler (`src/context.mjs`):**
   - DESIGN doesn't say which way priority runs. I chose: a higher number is kept longer, default 0, and on ties the later-declared input is cut first.
   - The budget is the smaller of the node budget and `classBudget`, counted over system plus prompt.
   - `</input` inside data is escaped so data can't close its block early.
   - A truncation is skipped if the marker would be bigger than the data. The receipt stays accurate, but that input can then exceed its `maxTokens`.
   - The receipt adds `declassifiedFrom` when a quarantined node declassifies.
   - `promptHash` is computed the same way as `promptHashOf` in `src/models/port.mjs`.
   - Extra exports: `contextInputs`, `inheritedLabel`, `joinLabels`, `estimateTokens`.
   - As DESIGN says, the output note is fixed text and doesn't include the schema; small models may need it.
3. **Verdicts (`src/verdict.mjs`):**
   - Each result also carries `authority`, `grantsActionAuthority: false` and `establishesCompletion: false`.
   - `cancelled` is not in the table; I mapped it to `inconclusive`.
   - A run that hasn't finished throws `RUN_NOT_TERMINAL`.
   - "network" is an explicit list of codes.
   - A confirmed finding is an entry in `findings` with `confirmed: true`, or a count passed in. The runtime integration needs to match this contract.
4. **Ports (`src/ports.mjs`):**
   - `EffectPort` keeps an in-memory idempotency record: a repeated key returns the first result, and the same key with different arguments is rejected.
   - It can take an allowed-capabilities list. Approvals stay in the runtime.
   - `JudgmentPort` results also include `costUsd` and `receiptHash`.
   - The model engine builds its prompt with `compileContext` as a quarantined node, and treats `state` as untrusted by default.
   - Probabilities are c·one-hot + (1−c)/n. `confidence` is the model's raw self-report.
5. **Schemas:**
   - `decision.schema.json` references the identity schema by its `$id`, so callers must load both with ajv.
   - `at` is epoch milliseconds.
   - `outcome.independence` adds `human` to DESIGN's three values.
   - The hash fields use `pattern`, so validating them through `compileDataSchema` needs `trustedSchema: true`.
6. **Schema subset (`src/schema-subset.mjs`):**
   - Violations raise `SCHEMA_NOT_PORTABLE`. It is a strict allowlist, so `title`, `$schema` and tuple `items` are rejected too.
   - Quarantined schemas also need `additionalProperties: false`, and every array needs `maxItems`.
   - `portableSchemaViolations` is already used by the sibling `src/models/port.mjs`.

**Remaining limits**
- When the host runs as root, Python code can still read root-readable files outside the hidden directories, such as `/etc/shadow`. JS code cannot.
- These hosts fail with `SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE` rather than running unsandboxed:
  - an interpreter installed under a hidden directory, such as nvm under `/home`;
  - mount points whose names contain escaped characters;
  - hosts where `unshare` or mounting a new `/proc` is blocked.
- Python has no memory or process-count limit beyond the wall-clock timeout.

**Integration notes.** I couldn't edit `package.json` or `src/engine.mjs`. The new schemas aren't in `package.json` "files", and the new modules aren't in the engine hash list yet.

Files are in /home/user/workflow-foundry:
- src/context.mjs
- src/sandbox.mjs
- src/verdict.mjs
- src/ports.mjs
- src/schema-subset.mjs
- schemas/identity.schema.json
- schemas/decision.schema.json
- tests/context.test.mjs
- tests/sandbox.test.mjs

result.integ:
The runtime now runs `agent`, `code` and `verify` nodes per DESIGN §1.1–1.3, §1.5, §5.1, §5.2 and §6. `npm test` is green: **713 tests, 696 pass, 0 fail, 17 skipped**. The baseline was 670 tests, 653 pass, 17 skipped. The 17 skips are the same opt-in and environment lanes as before, including the two `FOUNDRY_LIVE_MODELS=1` tests. All new tests use the scripted provider, so there were no network calls and no model spend. The new tests passed 3 out of 3 repeated runs.

## Files changed (all in /home/user/workflow-foundry; no commits by me)

| File | What changed |
|---|---|
| `schemas/workflow.schema.json` | Node kinds `agent`, `code`, `verify` with their fields and required-field rules (including per-`method` rules for verify); top-level `labels` and `discovery`. Additive; `schemaVersion` stays "1.0". |
| `src/validate.mjs` | `fields` for the new kinds; checks listed below; `validateIdentity` and `validateDecision`; exports `modelNodes`, `usesModel`, `VERIFY_RETURNS`. |
| `src/dataflow.mjs` | Output schemas: agent = `returns`, code = `returns` or unknown, verify = a fixed record. Inspects `subject`, context refs, and agent checks typed against `returns`. |
| `src/runtime.mjs` | Constructor options `{models, modelPolicy, codeRunner}`; run bindings in `create()`; the three node executors; verdict sealing; label propagation. |
| `src/store.mjs` | `decisions` table with `recordDecision`/`decisions(runId)`; `createRun` takes `id` and a whitelisted `binding` (hashes go into the `run.created` event); `updateRun` accepts several events. |
| `src/engine.mjs` | Engine identity now also covers `context.mjs`, `verdict.mjs`, `sandbox.mjs`, `schema-subset.mjs`, `models/port.mjs`, `models/policy.mjs`, `journal.mjs` and the identity/decision schemas. |
| `src/foundry.mjs` | Loads the committed model policy by default and passes it to validation and the runtime. Never creates a ModelPort itself. `createRun` passes through only `{modelMode, sampleSalt, assignment, identity}`. |
| `tests/engine-binding.test.mjs` | Existing test, outside my listed files. Its copy of the engine now uses `engineIdentity().files` instead of a hardcoded list; the assertions are unchanged. The `engine.mjs` change made this unavoidable. |
| `tests/runtime-agent.test.mjs` (new, 24 tests incl. subtests) | E1 retry then escalation; E2 escalate/resample/fail; E7 cap and `maxClass`; outages never escalate; cost budget; validation rejections; assignment; labels and quarantine; identity; policy drift; agent inside `map`; the Foundry wiring. |
| `tests/runtime-code-verify.test.mjs` (new, 14 tests incl. subtests) | Real-sandbox code → agent → python verify end to end; gate on and off; CODE_OUTPUT, CODE_ERROR, SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE, CODE_TIMEOUT; different-model enforcement (static and runtime); discovery findings; capability oracle. |
| `tests/runtime-replay.test.mjs` (new, 5 tests incl. subtests) | Replay with the same salt: zero provider calls and byte-identical receipts; replay miss; `replay-or-live` and fresh salts; two real SIGKILL crash recoveries, one killed before and one after the cost was charged, with no double charge. |

Validator checks added: agent `returns` must be in the portable subset (`SCHEMA_NOT_PORTABLE`), quarantined schemas must pass `QUARANTINE_SCHEMA`, and `MODEL_POLICY_REQUIRED` fires when model nodes exist without a policy. The model checks reject ids outside the policy (`MODEL_NOT_IN_POLICY`); classes are checked too, with errors MODEL_CLASS_UNKNOWN, MODEL_CLASS_MISMATCH, MODEL_CLASS_ORDER and MODEL_CLASS_EMPTY. The validator also enforces verify independence by method, `VERIFY_EFFECTS`, and the §4 `UNTRUSTED_EFFECT_ARGS` rule. Ref coverage now includes `context.inputs[].ref`, `checks` (with `output`), `subject` and `args`.

I did not edit `src/models/*`, `context.mjs`, `sandbox.mjs` or `verdict.mjs`. I edited `src/data.mjs` and then restored it; it is back to its pinned SHA-256 (`50049ae8…`). WIP commit a138166 captured the interim edit, and 158eba9 has the restored bytes.

## Deviations from DESIGN.md
1. **`output.*` in agent checks** is rewritten internally to `nodes._output.*`; no node id can start with `_`. I could not add an `output` root to `data.mjs`: outcome contracts store that file's SHA-256 and `outcome-history.mjs` pins it, so editing it breaks those checks. Side effect: dataflow messages name `nodes._output.x` rather than `output.x`.
2. **The `run.verdict` event comes just before** `run.succeeded`/`run.stopped`, in the same commit. `outcome-repair.mjs` and `outcome-history.mjs` require the terminal event to be last. A verdict is also sealed when an approval is rejected.
3. **New field `escalation.maxResamples`** (0..8, default 1). DESIGN says "resamples left" but names no field. When resamples run out, the node escalates under E2.
4. **`MODEL_PROTOCOL` and `MODEL_BUDGET` throw instead of escalating.** The pseudocode's "else → escalate" would hide provider faults. `MODEL_REFUSAL` still escalates under E1.
5. **Cost and steps.** Cost is charged after each call, keyed by journal id so recovery never double-charges. An overrun records the real spend, then stops with `COST_BUDGET`. Imputed cost is kept on node state and not charged to `run.cost`. Each agent node attempt counts as one step, not each call.
6. **Crash recovery replays the whole loop** with the same attempt, and ModelPort serves the calls already journaled. Events: `node.resumed`, then one `node.recovered_from_journal` per recovered call. Retry and escalation events are re-emitted marked `recovered:true`, and escalation decisions use fixed ids so the first record wins. The test-only fault hook is `extra.crashAfterModel=<nodeKey>`.
7. **Identity:** `foundry.policyHash` is `digest(run.policy)`, matching `run.created.policyHash`. The model policy hash is the separate `run.modelPolicyHash`. Callers may supply only the `arc` and `amp` parts.
8. **`modelPolicyHash` is recorded, and drift checked, only for workflows with model nodes**, so editing the policy does not block unrelated paused runs. A model run resumed by a runtime with no policy gets `MODEL_POLICY_REQUIRED`. If the stored hash disagrees with the creation event, it gets `MODEL_POLICY_BINDING_CORRUPT`.
9. **Assignment:** every key must name a model node and stay within its `maxClass` (`ASSIGNMENT_INVALID`). Escalation starts from the assigned model's class.
10. **Verify:**
    - Code and capability verifiers must be labelled `execution`; agent verifiers must not be.
    - Capability oracles must have no effects.
    - Code verifiers receive `{subject}` as input.
    - The agent verifier's fixed schema caps reasons at 8.
    - The subject reaches the model as a reserved `subject` context input.
    - `VERIFY_FAILED` error text leaves out the reasons, since they may come from untrusted data; they are kept in node state instead.
    - `different-model` is checked statically against the producers' initial families. At runtime the verifier is chosen, and escalates, excluding the families the producers actually used.
11. **Discovery findings:** DESIGN does not say how a finding is confirmed. I chose that each passing verify node in a `discovery:true` workflow appends a confirmed finding to `run.findings`.
12. **`onError:'continue'` on agent nodes** hides only model-behaviour failures. Outages, budget stops, cancellation, `REPLAY_MISS` and `VERIFY_INDEPENDENCE` always stop the run.
13. **Labels:** the outputs of code and task nodes take the label of their `args`; map and loop outputs join their children's labels. The untrusted-effect rule treats `requiresApproval` or `risk:'high'` as an approval gate, because the runtime already requires approval for both. The runtime repeats the check in `task()`.
14. **New error codes:** MODEL_POLICY_REQUIRED, MODEL_PORT_REQUIRED, MODEL_POLICY_BINDING_CORRUPT, MODEL_CLASS_ORDER, ASSIGNMENT_INVALID, RUN_OPTIONS, RUN_BINDING, VERIFY_INDEPENDENCE, VERIFY_EFFECTS, VERIFY_PROTOCOL, UNTRUSTED_EFFECT_ARGS, CONTEXT_INPUT.
15. **`inspectRun` is unchanged:** adding decisions to it broke the outcome-CLI deep-equality test. Decisions are read with `store.decisions(runId)`.
16. **Not done (outside this task):** §1.4 map `concurrency`/`failure`, and §5.4 timers.

## Open integration issues
- **Packaging:** `package.json` `"files"` (`src/*.mjs`) and the packaging test's `publicationPath` leave out `src/models/**` and the identity/decision schemas. A packed install would fail to load `engine.mjs` and `runtime.mjs`. The packaging end-to-end lane is opt-in, so the suite does not catch this; it needs an owner decision.
- **Other runtimes:** `trials.mjs` and `evaluation.mjs` create a Runtime without a model policy or ModelPort, so agent workflows cannot run through those paths yet.
- **Foundry has no ModelPort by default,** so agent runs started through it fail with `MODEL_PORT_REQUIRED` until the host wires one in.
